deals.description: With the next exhibition (opening tonight!) we again offer an extended program: Slide through all dates, join us for one of the curator's tours or save the first dates for 2027! 🌳 There are also a few last spots for the workshop with Beatrice Tulagan (19 Nov, 14:00!) – register via mail to ail@uni-ak.ac.at 🌳 AIL, Otto Wagner Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 (closed on public holidays, free entry) ail.angewandte.at About the exhibition 'Future on Trial. Between Unruly Evidence and Unfinished Climate Justice’: Contributions by: adO/Aptive, Beatrice Tulagan, Eline Benjaminsen, Elias Kimaiyo, Forensic Architecture, Jonas Staal, Paolo Cirio, Prin Rodriguez, Radha D’Souza, Valentino Skarwan Curators: Adriano Vinca, Camille Belmin, Elisabeth Falkensteiner Expert and scientific support: Inga Menke, Jameela Joy Reyes, Krishna Ariola, Michaela Krömer, Nicholas Petkov The engagement with climate justice reveals a complex field of perspectives across multiple temporalities, geographies, and forms of knowledge. In this context, environmental destruction is entangled with economic interests, the uneven distribution of risks and responsibilities, colonial continuities, imperialist power relations, and geological deep time. The exhibition Future on Trial. Between Unruly Evidence and Unfinished Climate Justice moves between two conceptions of justice. One that is produced and negotiated in courtrooms through scientific and legal evidence, data, and visual investigations, and another that understands justice as an unfinished, collective process, grounded in Indigenous knowledge, queer ecology, multispecies perspectives, and activism. Through a dialogue between artistic practices and scientific experts in the field of climate litigation, the exhibition opens up a space between evidence and uncertainty, accusation and repair, institutional accountability and collective imagination.
